messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital Course:
The 76-year-old woman with a medical history of cerebral infarction, endometrial cancer, and lumbar spine tumor was admitted to the Emergency Room with complaints of swelling, redness, and warmth on the left anterior chest wall. Physical examination and various medical tests revealed infectious arthritis in the left SCJ with multiple abscess pockets, small abscesses posterior to the left SCJ and sternum, and posterior to the clavicle. Treatment with the antibiotic cefazolin was started, but after two weeks, the antibiotic was switched to penicillin G due to the presence of Penicillin-sensitive Streptococcus agalactiae. However, the patient developed leukopenia and thrombocytopenia, which were suspected to be the side effects of penicillin. Cefazolin was then replaced by vancomycin and the treatment continued for another 2 weeks. After a total treatment duration of 6 weeks, the CRP level of the patient decreased to the normal range, and follow-up computed tomography of the chest showed improved SCJ swelling and abscess. The patient was discharged, and no signs of recurrence were observed after 3 months.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient was started on cefazolin empirically, targeting methicillin-susceptible S aureus (MSSA), which is the most common pathogen of SCJ septic arthritis. After identifying Penicillin-sensitive Streptococcus agalactiae, the treatment was switched to penicillin G for two weeks. Due to the side effects of penicillin, cefazolin was then restarted but later replaced by vancomycin.

Follow-Up Care:
The patient was discharged and lost to follow-up after 3 months.

Recommendations:
None

Signed,

[Date of discharge]

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The principal diagnosis is septic arthritis of the left sternoclavicular joint, caused by Streptococcus agalactiae.

In ICD-10-AM, pyogenic arthritis falls under M00 (M00.0 staphylococcal, M00.2 other streptococci, M00.8 other bacteria). The organism here is Streptococcus agalactiae, a group B streptococcus, so the category is M00.

M00
